title: Hybrid-precision attention cache + dynamic dequant path
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: Dequantization overhead and inconsistent kernel selection for mixed-precision attention are a growing source of tail-latency and cost on common inference workloads. For workloads that mix streaming decode and large prefill windows, repeated dequant/requant and unnecessary kernel switches increase per-token CPU/GPU work and introduce jitter. Goal: implement a hybrid-precision attention path that biases kernel selection toward quant-friendly variants when safe, caches per-layer precision decisions keyed by token distribution and sequence length, and optionally skip dequant on cached KV shards when numeric constraints are satisfied. This ticket covers design, a prototype kernel-level switch, validation microbenchmarks, and a small rollout plan to Canary cluster.
proposed_solution: Implement a per-model, per-layer precision score calculator that observes recent token distributions, max context, and scale histograms to decide INT8 vs FP8 vs FP16 for attention kernels.
Introduce a tiny KV-cache metadata header (cache-version + per-shard precision fingerprint) so decode can detect when cached KV is already in a usable quant format and skip an expensive dequant pass.

Add a kernel selector extension: when the layer precision score crosses threshold, route to quant-fused attention kernels that accept packed INT8/FP8 inputs and emit packed outputs without intermediate wide dequantization.

Fallback policy: if runtime underflow/overflow counters exceed safe limits or a downstream op requires full precision, automatically trigger a fast reclamation path that requants to FP16 for the next N tokens.
Instrumentation: expose token-level metrics (dequant_skipped_count, precision_switches, quant_fallbacks) and add microbenchmarks for 1B/7B/13B models across common sequence length profiles.
tradeoffs: Risk: packed-quant kernels reduce dequant work but increase complexity in cache metadata and kernel compatibility testing across hardware backends.
Safety: aggressive skipping of dequant may cause rare numeric quality regressions on adversarial input distributions; mitigated by conservative thresholds and automatic fallback.
Engineering cost: requires changes in serving runtime, cache format, and kernel ABI stubs which may increase maintenance burden until upstream kernels stabilize.
Benefit: expected 8-25% per-token GPU time reduction on quant-friendly workloads and substantial reduction in decode tail latency for mixed prefill/decode patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype implemented in runtime branch with a flag: runtime.quant_hybrid_attn = true.
Microbenchmarks show end-to-end token latency improvement >=6% for INT8/FP8 paths on representative 7B and 13B models with mixed prefill/decode profiles.
Cache-format change is backward-compatible: older runtimes ignore the new KV cache header without failing.
No quality regression on evaluation prompt set (bleu/rouge/semantic similarity) beyond predefined threshold (delta < 0.5% on critical evals).
Metrics exported: dequant_skipped_count, precision_switches, quant_fallbacks visible in Console for canary namespace.
Canary rollout completed to 5% traffic with automatic rollback if quant_fallbacks spike by >300% over baseline.

technical_notes: Cache header is intentionally compact: 8-byte fingerprint (xxhash64) + 1 byte precision bitmap + 1-byte version; version bump triggers full cache invalidation.
Precision score uses exponential moving average over per-token |scale| histograms and observed exponent clipping events to avoid thrashing.
Quant-fused attention kernel requires modified epilogue that accepts packed int8/4-bit scale metadata; we prototype with a shim that unpacks to FP16 only when required.
We reuse existing kernel fusion tests but add randomized quant noise tests and adversarial scale distributions to detect regressions early.
Hardware considerations: on A100 we see best gains for large sequence lengths; on H100 the FP8 path shows smaller wins but lower memory pressure—benchmarks must include both.
test_plan: Unit tests for cache header read/write and backward-ignore behavior.
Integration smoke tests for decode paths with and without cache hits that validate identical outputs within tolerance.
Performance regressions: run nightly microbench harness across 1B/7B/13B models and compare percentiles.
Canary validation harness that monitors quality metrics and global fallback rates; automatic rollback on thresholds.
